boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along College Avenue and Claremont Village corridors, each paired with one documented reason to step off campus.

cards.title: Meet California’s Native Flora
cards.subtitle: North College Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk north on College Avenue to explore an 86-acre living collection devoted exclusively to plants native to California.
cards.short_summary: An extensive native-plant collection immediately north of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: California Botanic Garden is an 86-acre living museum with curated collections of more than 22,000 California native plants at 1500 N. College Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Sunday; seasonal closing times apply. General admission is charged, with reduced student admission available with ID.

cards.title: Choose Your Park Activity
cards.subtitle: North Indian Hill Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Head to Indian Hill Boulevard for courts, picnic tables, a playground, bandshell, and the historic Garner House in one stop.
cards.short_summary: A multi-use community park with recreation and local history.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Memorial Park as a 7.2-acre community park with courts, picnic areas, a playground, bandshell, and historic Garner House.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 6:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. daily; individual facilities or scheduled activities may have separate availability.

cards.title: Study Beyond Mudd’s Buildings
cards.subtitle: North Dartmouth Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Follow Dartmouth Avenue to the consortium library; visitors can use street parking or request a temporary campus parking pass.
cards.short_summary: The consortium’s library anchors the Dartmouth Avenue academic corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Colleges Library is located at 800 N. Dartmouth Avenue, where Dartmouth meets Eighth Street.
cards.source_title: Directions & Parking – The Claremont Colleges Library
cards.access_notes: Entry and building-use rules can vary by affiliation and academic calendar; consult the library’s current hours and visitor policies before going.

cards.entity_name: Benton Museum of Art at Pomona College
cards.title: See Art at the Town–Gown Edge
cards.subtitle: West Bonita Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Continue to Bonita Avenue for a museum deliberately positioned where Pomona College meets Claremont’s civic center and Village.
cards.short_summary: A college art museum designed to connect campus and town.
cards.evidence_claim: The Benton Museum stands at 120 W. Bonita Avenue; Pomona describes its site at Bonita and College as connecting the campus with Claremont visitors.
cards.source_title: Brand-New Benton Museum of Art at Pomona College Opens Doors to Public
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s current visit page for public hours, admission details, accessibility information, and temporary closures.

cards.title: Handle Instruments from Around the World
cards.subtitle: North Yale Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Turn onto Yale Avenue for the center’s public look-touch-play experience featuring instruments gathered from around the world.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on musical-instrument shop and museum on Yale Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Folk Music Center & Museum at 220 Yale Avenue states that its mission is to offer the public a look, touch, and play experience with worldwide instruments.
cards.access_notes: The published schedule lists Tuesday noon–5:00 p.m. and Wednesday–Saturday 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; closed Sunday and Monday.

cards.title: Pick Up a Bakery Treat
cards.subtitle: South Yale Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Walk down Yale Avenue and choose in person from the bakery counter; special orders must also be placed at the shop or by phone.
cards.short_summary: A compact Yale Avenue stop for baked goods and counter orders.
cards.evidence_claim: Some Crust Bakery’s official contact page locates its shop at 119 Yale Avenue and says orders are placed in person or by telephone.
cards.access_notes: Consult the bakery’s current website before visiting; purchasing food or drink is required for the featured reason.

cards.title: Enter the Historic Depot for Art
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow First Street to the old depot and view regional art; bring student identification for the museum’s documented free admission.
cards.short_summary: A regional art museum housed inside Claremont’s historic depot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Lewis Museum of Art occupies the Claremont Depot at 200 W. First Street and provides free admission to students and visitors under 18.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit - Claremont Lewis Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: The museum is closed for installation through August 14, 2026. Check the visit page before going; students should bring ID for free admission.

cards.title: Catch the San Bernardino Line
cards.subtitle: West First Street rail corridor
cards.notes: Use the First Street depot platform for San Bernardino Line rail service and connections to local transit providers.
cards.short_summary: The Village’s regional-rail gateway occupies the historic depot corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Metrolink lists Claremont Station at 201 W. First Street on the San Bernardino Line, with Foothill Transit and local dial-a-ride connections.
cards.access_notes: Train travel requires a valid fare. Review the current station schedule and active service advisories before leaving campus.

cards.title: Explore a Citrus-Era Landmark
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor
cards.notes: Continue west on First Street to explore the restored 1922 packing building’s artisan shops, restaurants, classes, and public events.
cards.short_summary: A former citrus packing facility reused as a mixed commercial landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Packing House at 532 W. First Street describes itself as a historic Village landmark containing artisan shops, restaurants, arts, and classes.
cards.source_title: Home | Claremont Packing House | Dining & Retail
cards.access_notes: The building lists daily operating hours, but individual tenants maintain their own schedules and may require purchases or class fees.

cards.title: Browse Books That Fund Book Access
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor
cards.notes: Stop farther west on First Street to browse used books; shop proceeds help the nonprofit cover Prison Library Project shipping costs.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit bookshop whose sales support books for incarcerated readers.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Forum operates its bookshop at 586 W. First Street and says proceeds directly support Prison Library Project shipping costs.
cards.access_notes: Published bookshop hours are Thursday–Sunday, 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; purchasing a book is optional, while merchandise prices vary.
